title: Preassemble an ER32 collet into its eccentric clamping nut
objective: Orient a matching ER32 collet and clamping nut, place the collet extraction groove into the eccentric ring at the nut’s marked point, then tilt and roll the collet until it audibly and mechanically seats. Stop before tool insertion, threading onto a holder, or torque tightening.
success_conditions: The correct collet is retained continuously around the nut’s eccentric ring after both grippers release it for 3 seconds, and a light nondestructive withdrawal check does not separate it. The mark and initial groove entry must be used, with no direct axial forcing. Zero score for an unretained or inverted collet, substituting a scripted latch, threading the nut onto a holder before verified engagement, permanent collet deformation, nut damage, dropped parts, or teleport/state overwrite. Partial credit may recognize correct orientation and initial groove capture, but not false retention.
industrial_value: REGO-FIX specifies nut-collet preassembly as a required tooling-system step and warns that improper assembly can damage collet concentricity or destroy the nut. Hiteco documents industrial MTC electrospindles using ER32 tooling, supporting relevance to robot-associated machining equipment without claiming that arbitrary manufacturers’ internal retention geometries are interchangeable.
dexterity: High. The defining motion is a constrained eccentric-lip capture followed by a changing-axis tilt/roll and snap engagement, not connector mating or ordinary peg insertion.

asset_plan: Do not build from nominal ER32 envelope dimensions alone. Acquire one mutually compatible physical REGO-FIX ER32 collet/nut pair or manufacturer-authorized internal CAD, measure the marked eccentric ring, extraction groove, lip eccentricity, lead-in, and elastic deflection, and record provenance. First test whether the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1 rigid-contact model can reproduce correct marked-point entry, snap retention, wrong-angle rejection, removal resistance, and reset repeatability. If essential collet spring deformation cannot be reproduced without an already validated compliant model, reject the task rather than using a magic latch. YAM reach and fingertip clearance must be checked at full scale before demo work.
risk: Blocked, not selected. The acquired sources prove the sequence and consequence but do not expose the internal eccentric-lip geometry, permissible deformation, snap force, or a licensed downloadable ER32 nut/collet asset. The available Hiteco dimensions establish ER32 industrial equipment, not interchangeability with REGO-FIX retention geometry. Existing novelty records include unrelated push-fit-collet release tasks; this assembly objective appears mechanically distinct, but a complete synchronized submission review remains required.
